hypothesis: GEM-FUSE1: blind-magnetics detector (RTP edge strength × low relief) with H33-2 B=2 catalogue-pruned emission targets concealed faults missing from USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue
mechanism: RTP horizontal-gradient magnitude peaks where magnetically different blocks juxtapose; low relief suppresses mapped scarps (family B) and isolates blind candidates. Emission: Hessian ridge NMS (σ1.0) → top-K 0.0245×domain → score-ordered Poisson-disk 1.5 px → delete dots ≤2 px (200 m) of visible catalogue traces. Pruned shell earns <0.016 credit/dot vs 0.0556 break-even at DTI 0.2778 (live inversion), so its removal raises DTI by denominator reduction.
non_fault_process_that_could_mimic_it: Basin-margin facies changes and lithologic contacts produce RTP edges without a fault; low-relief sedimentary cover can mimic the blind-fault signature and earn no hidden truth credit. Also the catalogue-proximity credit deficit may not hold if hidden truth clusters near mapped traces (IR-32-PROXY-01).
